sources.title: Ghulam Muhammad Lakho, The Samma Kingdom of Sindh: Historical Studies
sources.note: Institute of Sindhology collection on origins, chronology, rulers, coinage, learning, literature, irrigation, monuments, and the dynasty ending.

sources.title: The Coinage and Genealogy of the Later Jams of Sind
sources.note: Peer-reviewed numismatic study of Jam Nizam al-Din, Jam Firuz, Jam Salah al-Din, titles, genealogy, chronology disputes, coins, and the dated tomb inscription.

sources.title: UNESCO, Historical Monuments at Makli, Thatta
sources.note: World Heritage synthesis on Thatta, Makli, Jam Nizamuddin, half a million graves, social groups, materials, and fused architectural influences.

sources.title: UNESCO and ICOMOS 2012 reactive monitoring mission to Makli
sources.note: Detailed World Heritage account of Makli monuments, Jam Nizamuddin, materials, river shift, climate, condition, and archaeological limits.

sources.title: Pakistan Department of Archaeology and Museums, Tomb of Jam Nizamuddin
sources.note: Official inventory describing the Samma tomb, unfinished dome, carved bands, inscriptions, balconies, floral forms, and Gujarat-linked craftsmanship.

sources.title: Pakistan Department of Archaeology and Museums, Jam Tamachi Ji Mari
sources.note: Official inventory separating the Nuri and Jam Tamachi story, competing grave traditions, fisher-community memory, and uncertain physical evidence.

sources.title: Endowment Fund Trust, Jamia Masjid at Makli
sources.note: Sindh heritage record of the large Samma brick mosque, Jam Tamachi, Shaikh Hammad Jamali, and the adjacent khanqah.

sources.title: Endowment Fund Trust, Samui, Thatta
sources.note: Sindh heritage record of the earlier Samma center, river-course change, perennial water, settlement shift, and cultivated land.

sources.title: Endowment Fund Trust, Nuri and Jam Tamachi at Makli
sources.note: Heritage description of the polygonal dressed-stone pavilion associated with Jam Tamachi, Nuri, and a child.

sources.title: Munazzah Akhtar, Interrogating the Dead: Makli Hill monuments
sources.note: University of Victoria doctoral study of Samma monuments, patronage, inscriptions, architectural evidence, contested attributions, and later chronicles.

sources.title: International Conference on Asian History, Culture and Environment, Makli paper
sources.note: National Institute volume on Samma Thatta, visual links, stone sources, monuments, Jam Firuz, and the phased Arghun takeover.

sources.title: Habibullah Siddiqui, Education in Sindh: Past and Present
sources.note: Institute of Sindhology history of Samma madrasas, curriculum, scholars, stipends, regional learning centers, logic, philosophy, law, and medicine.

sources.title: Pakistan Perspectives, resistance to Arghun rule in Sindh
sources.note: Scholarly article describing Samma agriculture, commerce, Darya Khan, Saavi canal excavation, Manchar-area dam work, and resistance after invasion.

sources.title: M. H. Panhwar, Six Thousand Years of History of Irrigation in Sindh
sources.note: Historical engineering study of Samma-era river channels, wells, water lifts, irrigation, crops, and later ecological change.

sources.title: The Global World of Indian Merchants, Cambridge sample
sources.note: Cambridge evidence for fifteenth-century Bhatia merchants from Thatta resident at Muscat and intensive maritime connections.

sources.title: South Asian merchant networks
sources.note: Cambridge synthesis locating Sindhi participation in overseas merchant diasporas from the fifteenth century and explaining network ties.

sources.title: Sohaib Baig, Indian Hanafis in an Ocean of Hadith
sources.note: UCLA dissertation on Sindhi legal scholarship, manuscripts, scholarly travel, Arabic and Persian learning, and Indian Ocean exchange from the sixteenth century.

sources.title: Encyclopaedia Iranica, Abhari, Makhdum
sources.note: Scholarly reference on a Herati traditionist migrating to Sindh about 1512, Gahan as a learning center, Darya Khan, writings, sons, and pupils.

sources.title: Sindh Culture Department e-library, Persian themes in Sindhi poetry
sources.note: Provincial cultural research on Samma-period Persian poets, vernacular forms, court links, and the evidentiary limits of surviving literature.

sources.title: University of the Punjab, Feminist Voice in Eighteenth-Century Sindh
sources.note: Peer-reviewed analysis of Shah Abdul Latif traditions, Nuri as fisherwoman and queen, social stratification, family loyalty, and later poetic memory.

sources.title: UNESCO, History of Civilizations of Central Asia, volume 5
sources.note: UNESCO history situating Babur, Kandahar, Shah Beg Arghun, Sibi, and the wider Central Asian pressures behind conquest of Sindh.

sources.title: Suhail Zaheer Lari, A History of Sindh
sources.note: Oxford University Press history of Samma succession, Tughluq intervention, Thatta, Jam Nizamuddin, Jam Firuz, and Arghun conquest.

sources.title: Indo-Persian historian and Sindho-Persian intermediary: Tarikh-i Masumi
sources.note: Peer-reviewed study of the first Mughal-era Persian history of Sindh and the interests shaping later accounts of the Sammas.

sources.title: Courtly Disposition, medicine at Deccan sultanate courts
sources.note: Cambridge contextual study of Islamicate and Indic medical traditions at neighboring fifteenth- and sixteenth-century South Asian courts.

sources.title: IUCN, World Wetlands Day at Keenjhar Lake
sources.note: Modern ecological and livelihood evidence for Keenjhar fishing communities, used only to explain continuing landscape importance, not medieval statistics.

sources.title: UNESCO and ICOMOS 2015 reactive monitoring mission to Makli
sources.note: World Heritage review of the original nomination, city and necropolis boundaries, archaeology, monument groups, documentation gaps, and conservation.

sources.title: Endowment Fund Trust, Syed Shah Murad Shirazi, Thatta
sources.note: Sindh heritage record of a later-Samma madrasa tradition, mosque, neighborhood, scholar family, and uncertain dates.

sources.title: C. Mabel Duff, The Chronology of India to the Sixteenth Century
sources.note: Reference chronology for Shah Begs 1520 victory, division of Sindh, Jam Firuz, Shah Hasan, and early Arghun succession.

sources.title: Australian National University, Mughal History in Sindh
sources.note: Doctoral historical study evaluating Persian chronicle dates and supporting a circa 1524 endpoint for the final Arghun takeover.

sources.title: M. H. Panhwar, History of Irrigation, Drainage and Flood Management in Sindh
sources.note: Historical engineering synthesis on the Samma period, irrigation stability, floodplain cultivation, maintenance, and later changes.

sources.title: The History of India as Told by Its Own Historians, Sindh extracts
sources.note: Translated Persian chronicle extracts and editorial comparison for Tughluq campaigns, Samma submission, and dynasty chronology.

proposedOverrides.name: Samma Sultanate of Sindh
proposedOverrides.summary: The Samma Jams ruled from Thatta, supporting Indus agriculture, Indian Ocean trade, learning, and Makli craft before a phased Arghun conquest.
